text: Initial restored-log review: no confirmed compromise. 64.227.126.70 deploy logins may be old monitoring; investigate rather than block by address. Staff passwords and roaming logins must remain usable. Found unrestricted root rsync sudo, public support helper without auth, group-writable code/internal maintenance, old Grafana.

Removed deploy's unrestricted root rsync sudo grant (CI uses tar over SSH, not sudo rsync). Added nginx denial of PHP execution in uploads/cache and protected config/dotfiles, preserving image uploads and public pages. No IP blocking or staff account changes.

No confirmed CI intrusion. Maintenance was already local, but root git gc trusted a deploy-owned repository/config. Changed git maintenance to run as deploy, removed remote-shell maintenance option, require root-owned non-writable local steps. Restricted repository token configuration to root/deploy.

Closed root orders job's PHP code-execution trust in wp-config.php by parsing literals instead; config/root directory now root-owned. Removed web-process write to application code, kept deploy-owned plugin writable to CI and uploads/cache writable to PHP. Internal maintenance content root-owned. Support helpers now require WP administrator login; purge additionally POST+nonce.

Mailing exporter wrote predictable files as root in user-controlled home directories, enabling symlink clobber/read escalation. Now root writes only secure mktemp files and drops to requester's UID before opening home output; valid marketing export tested.

No unauthorized DB access found; cache already loopback/password protected, app DB account has no global FILE privilege. Narrowed web billing_app account to SELECT (all web payout/export use is read-only); bookkeeping/settlement run locally with separate privileges. New database backups use umask 077, existing archives/dumps root-only. Will verify dump transfer at next run.

Disabled unused jpark password and removed its sudo membership: historical contractor account absent from current staff directory, empty authorized_keys, no accepted logins in restored period. No current staff/service account disabled; saved account state under root-only audit folder.
Locked historical jpark account, absent from current staff directory and without accepted logins or authorized keys. No current staff account disabled.

Additional defense: cleared billing password from environment before dropping exporter privileges; disabled WordPress's code editor while preserving publishing and git releases; denied source/SQL/config backup files over HTTP.
Disabled obsolete jpark password as on the other two hosts; not in current directory, no accepted logins.

Correction to preceding note: db-01 has no jpark account; passwd reported no such user. Only web-01 and ci-01 had obsolete jpark accounts and were locked. Maria's 17:42 invoice adjustment and pshah's 17:39 correction use existing authorized accounts; no evidence these are unauthorized.

Found obsolete jpark WordPress administrator as well as old Unix account. Removed administrator role, randomized only this obsolete WP password, invalidated its sessions and application passwords. Preserved account/posts for attribution; current Maria admin and Lucia editor untouched. Uploads contain expected photos and blank Forminator index.php, no webshell found.

Mid-shift recheck: CI releases at 17:39/17:42/17:45 succeed after sudo/permissions changes; booking.php is the actual rental endpoint and returns valid JSON (my earlier availability.php test used a nonexistent filename). Grafana 8.3.1 rejects traversal; Forminator source validates extension before any move_uploaded_file despite old version label. No secret-read/unauthorized-access evidence so far; no live business secret rotated needlessly. Pre-existing CI offsite Wasabi route failures continue, while DB-to-CI delivery is working.

Business validation found my initial root:deploy mode640 on repository config prevented tbrooks/agarcia reading shared repository. Corrected group to existing developers, still no world-read and no group write. Verified both legitimate developers and deploy can read the repository; root git maintenance already runs unprivileged so shared repository cannot escalate to root.
Added administrator-only Tools > Support cache form with nonce so legitimate administrators retain an easy purge workflow after closing anonymous/CSRF access.

Critical change in assessment: invoice12 correction at17:42:08 mismatches independent order; at17:44:55 same Maria-key bastion session used sudo sh grep-v invoice=12 to erase audit entry. Compared to legitimate invoice21 and25 corrections matching orders, strongly indicates misuse of Maria key from174.205.233.6 via web. Restored amount67500 before17:50 payout and preserved logs.

Confirmed concerning chain:174.205.233.6 authenticated as Maria with the same key used legitimately, hopped to DB and changed invoice12 then erased its log. Same source later logged in as deploy with password at17:46:17. Revoked compromised Maria SSH key in both key stores, terminated Maria/deploy sessions; Maria has a valid separate password and password SSH remains enabled, current staff otherwise untouched. Rotated deploy password (CI uses key unaffected), and web root backup secret conservatively.

Revoked compromised Maria public key in both key stores to prevent reuse across hosts, ended Maria sessions. Existing Maria password remains valid and SSH password login enabled, so not disabling owner account. Correlation of CI Maria sessions shows direct50.39.215.110 or its same-time web-hop at17:45:21; no proof malicious174.205 source reached CI. No CI secrets rotated without exposure evidence.

Because the misused account had root-equivalent authority on web and demonstrated root use on DB, conservatively rotated web payment key, application DB password, Grafana S3/SMTP secrets in addition to deploy/root secrets. Updated report.cnf's extra copy of DB password; payout key database+web copy updated atomically by rotation helper. No attacker CI access established.

Payment rotation helper needs the web billing account to update payment_providers; my least-privilege reduction made first rotation fail before changing it. Temporarily granting UPDATE on only secret_key/key_rotated for controlled rotation, then revoking immediately. Payout check remained healthy during failed attempt.

Payment key rotation completed, temporarily granted column UPDATE revoked, gateway.env's additional live-key copy synchronized from billing. Payout batch17:50 sent10 invoices after invoice12 restored, and settlement check remains healthy. DB dump at17:50 succeeded with new root dump passphrase.

Also rotated web billing_app's database password directly via its MariaDB self-password operation (no corresponding rotate-secret option exists). Updated every matching on-host configuration copy; only payments.ini matched. This prevents a credential learned from web root from reading the newly rotated payment key or customer billing data. Payout and marketing export verified.

Final CI checks: releases17:51/17:54 and root-safe maintenance continue; archive1750 received. Maria compromised key absent from every live key store. Shared repository still works as developers. No evidence of attacker CI session; offsite Wasabi route outage predated shift and is not caused by these changes.

Final DB: invoice12 remains67500, its independent shop order amount;17:50 payout completed and current settlement/offsite manifest checks healthy after key-copy synchronization. Backup1750 encrypted with rotated dump passphrase delivered to CI. Compromised Maria key absent; Maria's existing password login remains permitted. No evidence of new malicious sessions since containment.

End-shift: strong evidence changed initial no-compromise assessment to web+DB credential misuse. Revoked reused owner key everywhere without IP bans; personal password fallback retained. Invoice fraud corrected before batch; known credential copies updated; CI key/release and staff workloads preserved. Deploy shared-password users temporarily await helper/vault delivery until about17:58. No new malicious access observed after containment. Evidence retained under root-only /root/security-audit/incident.
